question: When processing an internal table with the statement LOOP AT itab… ENDLOOP, what system variable contains the current row number? A. sy-tabix B. sy-linno C. sy-index D. sy-subrc
discussion: Selected Answer: A When an internal table is processed using a LOOP AT structure, the system variable sy-tabix automatically stores the index (row number) of the currently selected table entry. The other variables (sy-linno, sy-index, and sy-subrc) serve different purposes, such as cursor position or return code. This variable is crucial for tracking progress within table operations. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: When does SAP recommend to use a sorted or a hashed table respectively? (Choose two.) A. A hashed table, when you read a single record and specify the complete key. B. A sorted table, when you read a subset in a loop and specify a part of the key from the left without gaps. C. A hashed table, when you read a subset in a loop and specify a part of the key from the left without gasp. D. A sorted table, when you read a single record and specify non-key fields.
discussion: Selected Answer: AB A. A hashed table, when you read a single record and specify the complete key. B. A sorted table, when you read a subset in a loop and specify a part of the key from the left without gaps. Hashed tables are ideal for near-constant-time access to a single record using the full key because of their hash algorithm. Sorted tables are recommended for fast sequential reading of a data subset by leveraging a highly efficient binary search using left-justified key fields. This choice maximizes performance by matching the table structure to the required data access pattern. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: What are some features of a unique secondary key? (Choose two.) A. It is updated when the table is modified. B. It is created with the first read access of a table. C. It is updated when the modified table is read again. D. It is created when a table is filled.
discussion: Selected Answer: AD The correct features of a unique secondary key in an ABAP internal table are A and D. Here is the three-line explanation in English: A. It is updated when the table is modified.D. It is created when a table is filled. A unique secondary key is defined upon table creation and built immediately when the table is populated with data. Crucially, the system automatically maintains the key, updating it whenever the primary table is modified (e.g., records are inserted, deleted, or changed) to ensure the index remains valid and unique. This differs from non-unique secondary keys, which can be lazy-created. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel
